papers.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
papers.abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

papers.title: Maximum Probability of Independence in Transitive Matroids
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E$, and suppose that the automorphism group of $M$ acts transitively on $E$. We show the following: if $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ are sampled independently from a distribution $p$ on $E$, then the probability that the samples are distinct and that $\{X_1,\ldots,X_K\}$ is an independent set in $M$ is quasi-concave in $p$ and maximized when $p$ is uniform. For $2\le K\le\rank(M)$, we characterize all maximizers by uniform total mass on the parallel classes and, in particular, show that the maximizer is unique and has global quadratic stability when $M$ is simple. As a corollary, for a random $K\times N$ matrix over a finite field with i.i.d.\ rows, uniform sampling from the nonzero vectors maximizes the probability of full row rank. Finally, we show that uniform sampling maximizes $\Prob\big(\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)\ge r\big)$, and hence also $\E\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)$, for every $L, r$.

papers.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
papers.abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.

papers.title: On the Concavity of R\'enyi Entropy and R\'enyi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the concavity of R\'enyi entropy and R\'enyi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for R\'enyi orders $\alpha\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $\sigma$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $\Omega=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a H\"older Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $\mu \in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (\mu)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $\sigma$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(\mu)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(\mu)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$. $\mu\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(\rho || \nu)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.

papers.title: Resolution of Vinzant's Conjecture on Phase Retrieval Injectivity
papers.abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times M}$ with $N=4M-5$ has independent standard complex Gaussian entries. We prove that the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by $A$ is injective is strictly smaller than $1$, and is $O(M^{-1})$ as $M\to \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in \cite{bandeira2026randomstrasse101}. The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular GPT6-Astra, GPT 5.6-sol, and the Rethlas system.

papers.title: Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher
papers.abstract:
Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial data in $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$. No restriction on the noise intensity is needed for $d=2$, while a smallness condition is required for $d\geq3$. The key new challenges arise from the thermal noise, which has a $(1+|
abla u|^2)^{1/4}$-type coefficient. This coefficient gives rise to an irregular Stratonovich-to-It\^o correction term of the form $
abla u\cdot D^2u
abla u/(1+|
abla u|^2)^{3/2}$. Our main innovation is a compactness argument tailored to the structure of the correction. By combining a factorization of this term with $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$ and area estimates, we establish strong convergence of the normalized gradients and reconstruct the weighted Hessian, which allows us to define the correction at energy regularity and identify its approximation limit.

papers.title: A stochastic chemical system in contact with reservoirs
papers.abstract: In this paper we analyse the behaviour of a non-reversible stochastic chemical system obtained as an approximation of a stochastic chemical system in which the concentration of some chemicals is higher than the concentration of the other chemicals. The master equation associated with this approximated system is characterised by a discrete part, modelling the reactions among chemicals that have low concentration, by a transport term and a diffusion term. The transport-diffusion terms describe the fluctuations in the concentration of abundant chemicals. The model contains a second order term is of order {\epsilon}, that describes the fluctuation in the concentrations of the abundand substances. We prove that the master equation has a spectral gap that is independent on $\epsilon$ and we analyse in detail the asymptotics of the solution to the master equation as $\epsilon \to 0$.

papers.title: Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
papers.abstract: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.

papers.title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.

papers.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
papers.abstract: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.

papers.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
papers.abstract: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.

papers.title: Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions along vector fields
papers.abstract: We investigate diffusion approximations for a class of multivariate inhomogeneous finite-velocity random motions motivated by models of active particles. A particle alternates cyclically among prescribed velocity fields $V_1,\dots,V_p$ with random run times and evolves according to either a \emph{flight} dynamics, consisting of piecewise-linear motion, or a \emph{gliding} dynamics, in which the particle follows the corresponding velocity flow. Under a Kac-type scaling that couples vanishing run times with diverging particle speed, we prove weak convergence of both processes to multidimensional diffusions. It turns out that the order of successive cyclic motions affects the diffusion limit. In addition to the second-order term generated by fluctuations of the random run times, the limiting drift contains directional derivatives $DV_i[V_j]$ of the underlying vector fields. In Stratonovich form, part of this drift is expressed through their Lie brackets $[V_i,V_j]$. Thus, the generic non-commutativity of the microscopic motions survives the diffusive scaling and generates a macroscopic drift which depends on the cyclic order. The limiting drift also distinguishes the flight and gliding dynamics, despite their being driven by the same vector fields and run times. Several examples, including run-and-reverse motion and cyclic dynamics generated by multiple vector fields, illustrate how the cyclic switching protocol and the geometry of the underlying velocity fields shape the limiting diffusions.

papers.title: Transforms between multivariate Laguerre and Meixner polynomials and their applications to gateways
papers.abstract: We establish gateways in both directions between the Laguerre process and a discrete Markov process for every inverse temperature $2\theta \geq 1$. Here, a gateway is an intertwining relation between Markov processes with continuous and discrete state spaces. A key ingredient is a pair of generating function identities that relate two double generating functions for multivariate Meixner polynomials to a single and a double generating function for multivariate Laguerre polynomials, respectively. These identities reveal a close relationship between the two families of polynomials and yield integral transforms that underlie the gateway relations. Gateway relations provide a means of transferring properties between continuous and discrete processes. As an application, we derive the Feller-Dynkin property and the uniqueness of the invariant distribution for the Laguerre process from the corresponding properties of the discrete process.

papers.title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
papers.abstract: Let $\gamma$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_\gamma$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_\gamma$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,\delta)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_\gamma$.

papers.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
papers.abstract: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.

papers.title: Cutoff for q-deformed classical card shuffles in the type A Iwahori--Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.

papers.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
papers.abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties. We also study the probability that a family of $N$ i.i.d.\ Gaussian points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in convex position and show that a sharp threshold occurs around the value $N=\exp(d/2e)$.

papers.title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
papers.abstract: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.

papers.title: Tail Asymptotics for Gaps in Unitary Ensembles and the Airy Point Process
papers.abstract: We derive tail asymptotics for the gap between the $k$th and $(k+1)$st largest particles, with $k$ fixed, in unitary ensembles and in the Airy point process. For the finite-$N$ ensembles, we consider the probabilities of a rescaled gap larger than $a_N$ and of a rescaled gap smaller than $b_N$, in the joint limits $N\to\infty$, $a_N\to\infty$ with $a_N=o(N^{2/3})$, and $N\to\infty$, $b_N\downarrow0$, respectively. For the Airy point process, the right and left tails are analyzed as the gap size tends to infinity and zero, respectively. More precisely, in both models, we obtain logarithmic right-tail asymptotics up to the constant term and cubic left-tail asymptotics with coefficient $k/6$. As an application, we also derive the limiting conditional laws of the leading particles given the existence of an abnormally large or small gap. In particular, for $k=1$, large-gap conditioning leads to a transition from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian fluctuations of the largest particle, similar to the BBP transition. Further, among any fixed number of leading gaps, we also determine the limiting probabilities of which gap attains a large maximum or a small minimum.

papers.title: Integration by parts and DLR equations for SPDEs on the whole line
papers.abstract: We study a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation on the whole real line, driven by space-time white noise, with a possibly nonlocal diffusion operator, such as a fractional Laplacian, and a coercive potential with polynomial growth. On the whole line, unlike on bounded intervals, its invariant measures cannot be described by an explicit density with respect to a Gaussian measure. We set the equation in suitable weighted spaces and show that invariant and infinitesimally invariant measures coincide, as do reversible measures and solutions to an integration-by-parts formula. We then show that the reversible measures are exactly the Gibbs measures defined through the Dobrushin-Lanford-Ruelle equations, without any moment condition, thanks to a priori estimates that also yield a Fernique-type theorem, uniform with respect to translations. In this way, we connect the Da Prato-Zabczyk approach to invariant measures of SPDEs with the DLR approach from statistical mechanics to Gibbs measures. Finally, we prove the existence of a reflection positive reversible measure and, in analogy with the one-dimensional long-range Ising model, we show that the reversible measure is unique, ergodic and translation invariant when the kernel of the nonlocal operator has a finite first moment, while it can be non-unique, for suitable double-well potentials, when the kernel has a power-law decay with infinite first moment.

papers.title: Composite local observables of sine-Gordon via stochastic analysis
papers.abstract: We develop a rigorous framework for the description of general local composite observables in Euclidean quantum field theories. The approach is nonperturbative and combines renormalisation group ideas with techniques of stochastic analysis. Via renormalisation dictated by sufficiently precise approximate solution theory of corresponding flow equations, we construct various local observables of the sine-Gordon model on the full space up to $\beta^2<6\pi$, including highly singular ones such as vertex fields $\exp(i\alpha\phi(y))$ in the optimal Wick regime $|\operatorname{Re}(\alpha)|<4\pi/\beta$ and derivatives of arbitrarily high order, i.e. $\partial^\mu\phi(y)$ for any multiindex $\mu\in \mathbb{N}^2_0$. Applications of the approach include a direct proof of smoothness of observable-inserted correlation functions, and verification that the constructed objects satisfy a version of the prefactorization algebra axioms adapted to our setting.

papers.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
papers.abstract: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. Two mechanisms compete: a collective upward displacement of the field, whose cost is governed by capacity, and the suppression of the remaining local violations, whose cost is their expected number, both of which are of order $N^{d-2}/\log N$ exactly in the window $h_N(\beta)^2=g_0(4\log N+\log\log N+2\beta)$. We obtain a sharp asymptotic rate expressed through a variational problem combining a Dirichlet energy with an exponential potential inside this critical window. Outside this window we obtain the asymptotics at the appropriate moving speeds: capacity alone governs the cost as $\beta\to-\infty$, and the expected number of violations as $\beta\to+\infty$. As an application, we derive lower-deviation bounds for the cover level of a macroscopic body by random interlacements, which determine the order of decay at the transition.

papers.title: Supercritical Liouville quantum gravity and CLE$_4$
papers.abstract: We establish the first relationship between Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) and Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) in the supercritical (a.k.a. strongly coupled) phase, which corresponds to central charge values $\mathbf c_{\mathrm L} \in (1,25)$ or equivalently to complex values of $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|=2$. More precisely, we introduce a canonical supercritical LQG surface with the topology of the disk. We then show that for each $\mathbf c_{\mathrm L} \in (1,25)$ there is a coupling of this LQG surface with a conformal loop ensemble with parameter $\kappa=4$ (CLE$_4$) wherein the LQG surfaces parametrized by the regions enclosed by the CLE$_4$ loops are conditionally independent supercritical LQG disks given their boundary lengths. In this coupling, the CLE$_4$ is neither determined by nor independent from the LQG. Guided by our coupling result, we exhibit a combinatorially natural family of loop-decorated random planar maps whose scaling limit we conjecture to be the supercritical LQG disk coupled to CLE$_4$. We include a substantial list of open problems.

papers.title: Bernoulli flow for Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix $A$ of the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph $\mathbb G(N,p)$ in the regime $Np \gg (\log N)^2$. We establish optimal isotropic delocalization for the bulk eigenvectors $\boldsymbol u$, meaning that $\langle \boldsymbol v, \boldsymbol u\rangle^2 \leq \frac{C \log N}{N}$ with very high probability for any deterministic normalized $\boldsymbol v$. In addition, we prove local spectral universality in the bulk by showing that the local spectral statistics coincide with those of the GOE. The main tool of our proof is a local law for the resolvent of $A$, down to optimal spectral scales and with optimal error bounds. Its proof relies on a new approach to local laws that we call the Bernoulli flow. It is a characteristic flow method in which the usual Brownian process is replaced by a Bernoulli process, where each edge of the graph forms an independent Markov process that jumps at unit rate from closed to open. The spectral parameter flows according to a suitably constructed matrix-valued Bernoulli characteristic flow.

papers.title: Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
papers.abstract: This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $\mu_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.

papers.title: Sharp and explicit Berry--Esseen inequalities over convex sets
papers.abstract: We establish finite-sample Berry--Esseen bounds over all convex subsets of $\R^{d}$ for sums of independent random vectors. The upper bounds give explicit dependence on the sample size, dimension, and moments of the summands, with numerical constants. They allow arbitrary dependence among coordinates and cover every real moment order from three onward. For i.i.d. summands, we determine the optimal dependence of the worst-case error on the sample size, the dimension, and the prescribed moment bound. We obtain matching lower bounds using bounded distributions that can be chosen independently of the sample size. The results reveal a fourth-moment threshold for normal approximation over convex sets. Four is the first moment order for which uniform bounds on the corresponding coordinate moments yield a worst-case error bound linear in the dimension. Bounds on higher moments give the same worst-case rate. The proof combines convexity with the addition of independent Gaussian noise to establish a normal approximation bound for Rademacher sums on Parseval frames. Random swaps with independent copies then allow us to apply this bound conditionally to general sums of independent random vectors.

papers.title: Bi-parameter local linearization and parameter estimation for the damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation with spatially colored noise
papers.abstract: Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation driven by Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space, with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$. For a globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient, we approximate characteristic mixed increments by those of the additive equation, multiplied by the coefficient frozen at the base point. A critical-kernel reduction and localized Riesz covariance estimates control the additional kernel terms and spatial correlations. We also establish $L^p$ error bounds for normalized quadratic variations and, under a nondegeneracy condition, construct jointly strongly consistent estimators of the Hurst parameter and a positive diffusion parameter.

papers.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,\alpha}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,\alpha}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.
